record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every graph G with m edges and minimum degree at least 2 admit a bisection (S, T) such that each of the two induced subgraphs G[S] and G[T] contains at most m/3 edges?

evidence.quote:
Conjecture 3.1[13, Conjecture 6] Every graph with m edges and minimum degree at least 2 admits a bisection of which each vertex class induces at most m
3 edges.
Employing also the idea of free neighbors from [40], Xu and Yu[71] confirmed Conjecture 3.1 and characterized the extremal graph.

Theorem 3.6[71] Every graph with m edges and minimum degree at least 2 admits a good bisection, i.e., a bisection (S, S¯) such that max{e(S), e(S¯)} ≤ m
3 . Moreover, the triangle K3 is the only extremal graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with $m=|E|$ edges and minimum degree at least $2$. A bisection of $G$ is an ordered partition $(S,T)$ of $V$ with $||S|-|T||\le 1$. For a vertex set $X\subseteq V$, let $e(X)$ denote the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $X$. Prove or disprove: every such graph $G$ admits a bisection $(S,T)$ satisfying \[ \max\{e(S),\,e(T)\} \le \frac{m}{3}. \] Moreover, determine all graphs for which equality is achieved.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (originally posed by Bollobás and Scott) was confirmed by Xu and Yu, who proved that every graph with m edges and minimum degree at least 2 admits a bisection (S,T) with max{e(S),e(T)} ≤ m/3, and characterized the triangle K_3 as the unique extremal graph.
